visible_to_student.context: Fourth-year student, feels constant tension and fear of making mistakes.
visible_to_student.setting: First consultation at the university psychological center
visible_to_student.initial_request: "I constantly worry, even when everything is objectively fine."
visible_to_student.warning_to_student: Tends to be self-critical and perfectionistic; it's important not to rush to reassure.

hidden_for_student.provisional_diagnosis: Generalized anxiety disorder (GAD) with mild depressive features
goals_for_training: Mastering skills for establishing safe contact with an anxious client.
Developing the ability to explore the content of anxious thoughts, not just their intensity.
Practicing structuring the first session in the context of high background anxiety.
hidden_for_student.notes_for_teacher: The client often talks about the fear of 'letting others down'; it is useful to explore her internal standards and expectations.

personality_style.description: Perfectionist, approval-oriented, tends to overthink and worry about the future.

typical_phrases: I always feel like I'm missing something.
Even when everything is done, I think I could have done better.
I can't just relax; my mind won't turn off.
It seems like nothing terrible is happening, but the anxiety doesn't go away.

visible_to_student.context: Works in an office, has two children, complains of constant worries about family and work.
visible_to_student.initial_request: "I'm always waiting for something to happen to my children or at work."
visible_to_student.warning_to_student: May undervalue her own needs, focusing only on caring for others.

goals_for_training: Practicing the skill of exploring the distribution of responsibility and boundaries.
Helping the student maintain empathy when faced with complaints about 'endless burdens.'
Finding resources and supports, not just problems.
hidden_for_student.notes_for_teacher: The client may say that 'it's shameful to complain'; it's important to recognize her fatigue and normalize her request.

personality_style.description: Very caring, used to 'carrying everything,' feels ashamed to ask for help.

typical_phrases: If I relax, something will definitely happen.
I have no right to 'drop out'; everyone depends on me.
It's hard to believe that everything will be okay if I don't control everything.

visible_to_student.context: Works in an office, has called an ambulance several times due to panic attacks.
visible_to_student.initial_request: "Sometimes it suddenly hits me: my heart races, I feel like I'm dying."
visible_to_student.warning_to_student: It's important not to undervalue physical symptoms and not to take on the role of a cardiologist.

goals_for_training: Mastering detailed questioning about the first and subsequent panic attacks.
Understanding the role of avoidance and anticipatory anxiety.
Practicing psychoeducation about panic without making promises of 'cure forever.'
hidden_for_student.notes_for_teacher: The client believes the problem is with his heart; it's important to gently connect the physical and psychological without arguing directly.

personality_style.description: Controlling, dislikes appearing weak, perceives anxiety as a weakness.

typical_phrases: I know for sure that something serious is happening to me at that moment.
Doctors say everything is fine, but it feels different.
I've started avoiding the subway and shopping malls.
I'm scared that this will happen in a crowded place and I'll be embarrassed.

visible_to_student.context: Recently moved to another city; attacks started after changing jobs.
visible_to_student.initial_request: "Suddenly my head starts spinning, my vision darkens, I'm afraid I'll faint."
visible_to_student.warning_to_student: There is a connection to the stress of moving; it's important to consider the context, not just the symptoms.

hidden_for_student.provisional_diagnosis: Panic attacks in the context of adaptation stress
goals_for_training: Practicing the connection between life events and panic.
Understanding the role of avoidance and safe behaviors.
Practicing building a safety base in current life.
hidden_for_student.notes_for_teacher: The client may link everything only to physiology and fatigue; it is useful to delicately broaden the focus.

personality_style.description: Sensitive, prone to doubts, seeks support in relationships.

typical_phrases: I'm afraid I'll faint and no one will help me.
Since I moved, my anxiety has increased a lot.
Sometimes it's scary to leave the house without someone by my side.

visible_to_student.context: Works in IT, fears contamination and infection, constantly washes her hands and home.
visible_to_student.initial_request: "I know this is excessive, but if I don't wash, my anxiety skyrockets."
visible_to_student.warning_to_student: Do not reinforce rituals and avoid enhancing checks.

goals_for_training: Differentiating obsessions from real risks.
Practicing tolerating the client's anxiety without immediate reassurance.
Understanding the dynamics of 'thought - anxiety - ritual - relief.'
hidden_for_student.notes_for_teacher: The client rationally understands the excessiveness of her behavior but emotionally cannot withstand refraining from rituals.

personality_style.description: Responsible, meticulous, fears 'making a mistake' and causing harm.

typical_phrases: I can wash my hands for half an hour until I feel that it's 'enough.'
I know the chances of infection are small, but the anxiety is very strong.
I often refuse to meet if it seems that it will be dirty there.

visible_to_student.context: Engineer, spends a lot of time checking locks and appliances.
visible_to_student.initial_request: "I check the door and the stove ten times; otherwise, I can't leave."
visible_to_student.warning_to_student: It's important not to become another source of reassurance that 'everything is fine.'

hidden_for_student.provisional_diagnosis: OCD, dominated by checking and responsibility for harm
goals_for_training: Explore the connection between the sense of responsibility and rituals.
Practice a resilient non-reassuring style.
Understand how rituals interfere with daily functioning.
hidden_for_student.notes_for_teacher: The client may justify checking with 'common sense'; it's important to gently guide them to the cost in terms of time and tension.

personality_style.description: Tends to control and feel responsible, fears doing something 'wrong.'

typical_phrases: If I don't check, I'll think about it all day.
Sometimes I go back home just to make sure everything is turned off.
I feel like if something happens, it will be my fault.

visible_to_student.context: Experienced a serious car accident a year ago, avoids cars, troubled by dreams and memories.
visible_to_student.initial_request: "I dream about the accident at night, and during the day I avoid any roads."
visible_to_student.warning_to_student: Be cautious when asking about the details of the trauma; it's important not to re-traumatize.

goals_for_training: Develop skills to work with avoidance and hyperarousal.
Learn to tolerate pauses and the client's emotional reactions.
Practice gentle entry and exit from the trauma topic.
hidden_for_student.notes_for_teacher: The client may 'get stuck' in describing details or become detached.

personality_style.description: Reserved, has become even more closed off and cautious after the trauma.

typical_phrases: I keep replaying that moment, even though I want to forget.
I feel like I'm not the person I was before the accident.
People say, 'be glad you're alive,' but I feel like I'm stuck there.

visible_to_student.context: Experienced violence in an intimate relationship, seeking help two years after the breakup.
visible_to_student.initial_request: "I tried to forget, but I still fear intimacy and conflict."
visible_to_student.warning_to_student: High sensitivity to the topic of trust and boundaries; it's important not to rush the disclosure of details.

goals_for_training: Sensitivity to the topic of violence and shame.
Practice establishing boundaries and the client's control over what to share.
Understand the impact of trauma on trust and intimacy.
hidden_for_student.notes_for_teacher: The client may blame herself; it's important to gently normalize and separate responsibility.

personality_style.description: The experience of violence has heightened the sense of insecurity in relationships, but the need for closeness remains.

typical_phrases: I seem to understand that I'm safe now, but my body reacts as it did then.
I find it hard to trust, especially if someone is angry or raises their voice.
I often think that it's my fault that things turned out this way.

visible_to_student.context: Student, frequently changes partners, complains of emptiness and sharp mood swings.
visible_to_student.initial_request: "I either idealize people or hate them, and it's like that with everyone."
visible_to_student.warning_to_student: There may be sudden changes in attitude towards the therapist; it's important to endure.

goals_for_training: Learn to tolerate the client's intense emotions without rushing interpretations.
Explore the fear of abandonment and attachment instability.
Practice responses to potential devaluation by the therapist.
hidden_for_student.notes_for_teacher: Past episodes of self-harming behavior, currently only thoughts; it's important to observe without detailing methods.

personality_style.description: Very sensitive to distance, fears being abandoned, extremes in relationships.

typical_phrases: I either cling to a person or push them away immediately.
Sometimes I don't even understand who I am and what I want.
If I don't get a response for a long time, I'm sure I'm being abandoned.

visible_to_student.context: Works, occasionally ends relationships, complains of anger outbursts and emptiness.
visible_to_student.initial_request: "Sometimes I feel nothing, and other times I want to destroy everything."
visible_to_student.warning_to_student: There may be casual mentions of 'not living'—it's important to ask carefully without detailing methods.

goals_for_training: Practice calm inquiry about self-harming thoughts.
Master the skill of tolerating the client's anger without becoming defensive.
Understand the connection between feelings of emptiness and impulsivity.
hidden_for_student.notes_for_teacher: The client may dramatically talk about 'extreme measures'; it's important to keep the focus on feelings and needs.

personality_style.description: Struggles with impulse control, conflict between the desire for closeness and the fear of rejection.

typical_phrases: When someone leaves me, it feels like I'm destroying myself.
I can say things in anger that I later deeply regret.
Sometimes I think everyone would be better off without me, but I don't do anything about it.

visible_to_student.context: Freelancer, feels undervalued, reacts painfully to criticism.
visible_to_student.initial_request: "I am surrounded by incompetent people, and it hinders my potential."
visible_to_student.warning_to_student: Devaluing comments towards the therapist may occur.

goals_for_training: Skill in enduring devaluation and inflated demands.
Understanding the dynamics of shame and vulnerability behind grandiosity.
Developing the ability to see the fear of inadequacy behind complaints.
hidden_for_student.notes_for_teacher: The client may test the student's competence; it is important to maintain a professional stance and interest.

personality_style.description: Demonstrates confidence outwardly, but fears being 'ordinary' and insignificant inside.

typical_phrases: It's hard for me to communicate with people who don't measure up to my level.
When I'm pointed out my mistakes, it feels like I've been completely devalued.
Sometimes it seems like no one sees how truly promising I am.

visible_to_student.context: Successful in her career, complains that partners 'do not measure up to her level.'
visible_to_student.initial_request: "I am constantly disappointed in people; there are few worthy ones around."
visible_to_student.warning_to_student: May try to dominate the conversation; it is important to maintain structure.

goals_for_training: Confronting devaluation without resorting to defensive responses.
Exploring themes of shame and loneliness behind grandiosity.
Skill in maintaining contact when the client shows little interest in the therapist as a person.
hidden_for_student.notes_for_teacher: May quickly resort to sarcasm when discussing vulnerable topics.

personality_style.description: Vibrant, charismatic, prone to dominating and criticizing others.

typical_phrases: I invest in people more than they deserve.
If someone can't appreciate me, that's their problem.
I rarely meet those who are truly on my level.

visible_to_student.context: Works in a creative field, complains of forgetfulness and difficulties with organization.
visible_to_student.initial_request: "I keep losing everything, I'm late, and I can't finish tasks."
visible_to_student.warning_to_student: It is important not to reduce this to 'laziness' but to see real functional difficulties.

goals_for_training: Focus on specific examples of attention and planning impairments.
Practice a normalizing, non-judgmental stance.
Distinguish between ADHD and simple procrastination.
hidden_for_student.notes_for_teacher: Uses humor as a defense, may devalue her difficulties.

personality_style.description: Energetic, creative, quickly gets excited, but struggles to maintain focus.

typical_phrases: I have a million ideas, but everything falls apart during the implementation stage.
I constantly forget important things and then feel terrible shame.
I can super-focus on something interesting and completely fail at everything else.

visible_to_student.context: Student, complains about the inability to sit through classes and concentrate.
visible_to_student.initial_request: "I sit in lectures and my mind drifts away in five minutes."
visible_to_student.warning_to_student: May use defensive humor; it is important not to become 'the second adult who scolds.'

goals_for_training: Distinguish between ADHD symptoms and 'just restlessness.'
Understand the impact of ADHD on studies and self-esteem.
Create a space where the client does not feel 'lazy.'
hidden_for_student.notes_for_teacher: May say he is 'just lazy,' but often shame is hidden behind this.

personality_style.description: Lively, humorous, but with a feeling that 'something is always wrong.'

typical_phrases: No matter how hard I try, I still get distracted.
Professors think I don't care, but I really do try.
I do my homework the night before it's due, even though I promise myself to start earlier.

visible_to_student.context: Student, performs well academically but avoids contact and quickly tires from socializing.
visible_to_student.initial_request: "I don't understand how to communicate with people, and I get tired from it."
visible_to_student.warning_to_student: It is important to speak clearly and structurally, avoiding double meanings.

hidden_for_student.provisional_diagnosis: Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) without intellectual disability
goals_for_training: Adapt speech style to the characteristics of ASD.
Understand the role of sensory overload.
Practice specific, predictable formulations of questions.
hidden_for_student.notes_for_teacher: May seem cold or indifferent, but experiences tension inside.

interpersonal_domain.attachment_style: more secure, but limited social circle

personality_style.description: Concise, direct, values honesty and predictability.

typical_phrases: I often don't understand what is expected of me in social situations.
When it gets too loud, I just want to leave.
It's easier for me when there are clear rules and communication scripts.

visible_to_student.context: Interested in psychoeducation, recently learned about autism spectrum disorder, feels 'different'.
visible_to_student.initial_request: "I find it hard to understand hints and maintain small talk."
visible_to_student.warning_to_student: It is important not to reduce everything to a diagnosis; consider the individual's personality.

hidden_for_student.provisional_diagnosis: Suspected autism spectrum disorder; psychiatric evaluation required.
goals_for_training: Understand the boundary between psychologist and psychiatrist competencies.
Practice gentle discussion of 'labels' and identity.
Develop respect for the client's uniqueness.
hidden_for_student.notes_for_teacher: The client may use internet terminology; it is important not to argue but to explore their experience.

personality_style.description: Intellectually curious, tends to analyze herself, feels different from the 'norm'.

typical_phrases: I feel like I'm saying it 'wrong', but I don't understand how to say it right.
After socializing, I need a long time to recover.
I found many descriptions of autism spectrum disorder online that resonate with me.

visible_to_student.context: Under observation, taking medication, complains of distrust towards people and strange sensations.
visible_to_student.setting: Outpatient care at a mental health clinic
visible_to_student.initial_request: "Sometimes it feels like I'm being watched, even though I understand it might just be in my head."
visible_to_student.warning_to_student: Do not argue with the experiences; it is important to gently explore.

hidden_for_student.provisional_diagnosis: Schizophrenia, episode in history, in remission.
goals_for_training: Practice non-judgmental interest in psychotic experiences.
Skill in reality anchoring without direct confrontation.
Consideration of fatigue and cognitive difficulties.
hidden_for_student.notes_for_teacher: May be sensitive to hints of 'abnormality'.

personality_style.description: Withdrawn, cautious, tries to control speech to avoid appearing strange.

typical_phrases: Sometimes it seems like people exchange glances when I walk in.
I understand that it might just be my thoughts, but it feels real.
After the last episode, I became more cautious in social interactions.

visible_to_student.context: Recently discharged from the hospital, currently stabilized, still experiencing strange sensations.
visible_to_student.initial_request: "Sometimes it feels like my thoughts are not entirely my own."
visible_to_student.warning_to_student: It is important not to be frightened by unusual expressions; maintain contact and support.

differential_diagnosis: Severe affective disorder with psychotic symptoms
goals_for_training: Skill in working with vulnerability after a psychotic episode.
Sensitivity to the topic of stigma and self-relationship.
Building supportive, non-pathologizing formulations.
hidden_for_student.notes_for_teacher: The client may feel ashamed of her diagnosis; it is important to avoid labels.

personality_style.description: Shy, sensitive, worried about her diagnosis and how people might perceive her.

typical_phrases: Sometimes it's hard to distinguish between just thoughts and something strange.
I'm afraid that if people find out about my diagnosis, they will treat me differently.
I try not to overload myself, but I feel disconnected from others.

visible_to_student.context: Lives with a partner, complains of 'outbursts' and feelings of shame afterward.
visible_to_student.setting: Psychological consultation at the request of the partner
visible_to_student.initial_request: "Sometimes it feels like I lose control, and then I feel ashamed."
visible_to_student.warning_to_student: It is important not to take an accusatory stance, but to explore.

hidden_for_student.provisional_diagnosis: Impulsive outbursts of aggression (intermittent explosive disorder - under question).
goals_for_training: Explore triggers and early signs of anger.
Separate responsibility for behavior from empathy for feelings.
Work on feelings of shame after outbursts.
hidden_for_student.notes_for_teacher: There are episodes of throwing objects, without intentional physical harm to others.

personality_style.description: Impulsive, hot-tempered, feels intense shame for his words and actions after outbursts.

typical_phrases: In the moment, I feel like I have no control, and then I think: why did I do that?
I don't want to be like my father, but sometimes I behave the same way.
My partner is afraid of my outbursts, and I'm also scared that I might say something I regret.

visible_to_student.context: Complains of sharp verbal outbursts in relationships and feelings of guilt afterward.
visible_to_student.initial_request: "When I'm provoked, I say terrible things, and then I feel very ashamed."
visible_to_student.warning_to_student: It is important not to indulge in self-criticism, but to explore the dynamics.

hidden_for_student.provisional_diagnosis: Episodic dysregulation of anger against a background of emotional vulnerability.
goals_for_training: Distinguish normal anger from maladaptive expressions.
Understand how early experiences influence current expressions of aggression.
Skill in compassionate positioning without justifying aggression.
hidden_for_student.notes_for_teacher: Often after outbursts, there is a period of self-criticism and attempts to 'make amends'.

personality_style.description: Sensitive to injustice, may react sharply, but then feels deeply troubled.

typical_phrases: I say things that I feel ashamed to even think about.
Then I try to fix everything, but the residue remains with everyone.
I'm afraid that at some point, people will just stop tolerating me.
